Bransk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Brańsk, Poland

Not demolished. Brańsk, granted town rights around 1440 and Magdeburg Law by the late 15th century, initially barred Jewish settlement - early Jewish leaseholders belonged to Tykocin's kehilla until the ban lifted in the early 19th century, with an independent community forming by 1820. Population reached 58% (2,400) by 1897, still about 50% (2,700) by 1939. Germans established a ghetto in fall 1941; its November 1942 liquidation ended with the last group of Jews shot directly at this cemetery, while the rest were deported in stages to Treblinka. The cemetery, likely founded at the start of the 19th century, has distinct old and new sections; in fall 1942, 70 people (mostly Jews) were shot here, commemorated with a 1968 monument. Since 1989, recovered tombstones from the town have been gathered into an on-site lapidarium; a 2017 obelisk was funded by the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage and the Sofer family of Houston, Texas.
